failure_modes.what: The manual «Κλείσιμο δρομολογίου — χειροκίνητο» button on TRIP PnL PATCHes /costs/rt/:id with only {status:'closed'} (modules/costs.js:812-815). The Worker's PATCH /costs/rt/:id handler (worker/src/index.js:3249-3261) applies it with no check that every leg's order is Delivered/Cancelled — canRemoveLeg (worker/src/rt-rules.mjs:136-141) guards leg DELETE, and trg:ct_rt_legs.rt_reopen_on_leg (045) reopens an already-closed RT when a NEW leg is later attached, but nothing stops the CLOSE itself while an existing leg is still open. The equivalent automatic-close path in core/rt-feed.js (team α) explicitly checks _rtOpenLegs before sending the same PATCH (core/rt-feed.js:439) — the manual button in my own file skips that check entirely.
failure_modes.gap: Nobody sees anything wrong at the moment of the click — the RT just becomes 'closed' (200 OK, toast implied by ctCloseAll()/ctReload()). It surfaces only if/when someone runs the B-02 SQL (not scheduled — no pg_cron exists, 02b §1.6) or if a later leg attachment triggers 045's reopen (which fixes the status but leaves an unexplained audit gap in between).

failure_modes.what: When the accountant decides 'delete_manual' for a duplicate manual/import pair during a DKV import, the Worker deletes the manual ct_cost_lines row AFTER the import insert succeeds (worker/src/index.js:4010-4029). If that DELETE fails (fetch error, transient 5xx), the id is pushed to manualDeleteErrors (line 4020,4026) but the commit still returns 201 with the import fully written. The response DOES carry manual_delete_errors (line 4090), but modules/expenses_import.js#eiCommit (lines 1155-1161) only reads res.manual_deleted (a count) to build its success toast — res.manual_delete_errors is never inspected or shown.
failure_modes.gap: The accountant sees 'Καταχωρήθηκαν N γραμμές · σβήστηκαν M χειροκίνητες διπλές' and believes the duplicate is gone. If the delete actually failed, the old manual line and the new imported line both live in ct_cost_lines — double-counted in ct_v_rt_costs/ct_v_rt_pnl and, if pay_source=CASH, double-summed into dl_entries.expenses by dbfn:dl_cash_sync. No B-check specifically looks for 'two lines with the same twin signature both still alive' — B-24 (dkv_dup_after_038) only catches duplicates that share a doc_id+rt_id+toll_country group, not a manual-vs-imported pair.

failure_modes.what: ctFetch (modules/costs.js:36-64), shared by every screen in this part, throws new Error('HTTP '+res.status) on a non-OK response with no JSON error body (line 55) and has NO special handling for 401 — unlike the facade's atPatch/_atRetry (core/api.js, team ε/α) which clears tms_user/tms_jwt and redirects to index.html.
failure_modes.gap: Already named generically in docs/grok-bot/monitoring-2026-09-22/02a-ροές-frontend.md F-02 ('HTTP 401' shown verbatim); confirmed here with the exact owning file. The user sees a raw 'HTTP 401' or 'Σφάλμα: HTTP 401' alert/card on Expenses/Payroll/TRIP PnL instead of being routed back to login — not silent (an error IS shown) but unexplained, and the expired session forces a manual reload to recover.

failure_modes.what: dl_cash_sync(rt) (worker/migrations/042_cash_lines_to_payroll.sql:66-102) selects the RT's live 'trip' dl_entries row and returns immediately, doing nothing, if none exists (line 73-74: 'if e.id is null then return; -- no live payroll line: dl_v_rt_gap already says so'). A CASH ct_cost_lines row can therefore be entered on an RT that currently has no ledger line (e.g. the RT briefly lost its driver, or the line was entered before the trg:ct_round_trips.dl_sync_from_rt trigger ever ran) with zero effect on payroll.
failure_modes.gap: The comment's own justification ('dl_v_rt_gap already says so') is only true if someone is actually watching dl_v_rt_gap (B-04) AND separately knows to look for CASH lines on those specific gapped RTs — B-07 (dl_cash_mismatch) explicitly excludes CASH lines with no matching dl_entries row from its comparison (02b.md:167 'Εξαιρ.: γραμμές CASH χωρίς rt_id — δεν φτάνουν ποτέ στη μισθοδοσία' covers no-rt_id, not no-live-entry), so a CASH line on a gapped RT is invisible to both B-04 (which only counts RTs, not orphaned cash) and B-07 (which requires a dl_entries row to compare against in the first place).

failure_modes.what: Mass payment (modules/payroll.js:1508-1529) POSTs one /costs/ledger entry per driver sequentially and stops at the first failure, by explicit design (comment 1506-1507: earlier successful rows stay). The UI is honest about this (per-row ✓/✕, footer message) — but no batch_id or client-generated correlation id is sent in any of the POST bodies.
failure_modes.gap: In the moment, the accountant/owner sees exactly which rows succeeded. Afterward, nobody — not audit_log, not any B-check — can reconstruct 'these N dl_entries rows were one mass-payment run of M intended, stopped early' without matching timestamps by hand. Confirms the gap already named in 02a F-35.

failure_modes.what: worker/src/index.js:3333-3335 filters rows where category==='cash_m' out of the response for any non-owner role. 'cash_m' was removed from CT_CATEGORIES and the ct_cost_lines_category_check CHECK constraint by migration 011 (worker/migrations/011_driver_ledger.sql:271-273; comment at index.js:2960-2963 confirms 'driver_pay and cash_m left this list on 2026-09-05'), so no row with that category can exist anymore.
failure_modes.gap: Not a runtime bug today (dead code, principle 8) — but it sits directly on the money-read path every accountant/management view of Έξοδα Δρομολογίων goes through, and a future re-introduction of a similarly-named category (or a copy-paste of this filter pattern onto a live category) would silently hide real cost lines from non-owner roles with no error anywhere.
